title: What Happens If You Drink Too Much Water?
sources: Cleveland Clinic, 'Water Intoxication' (more water in your body than you need; in some people symptoms can develop after drinking about a gallon (3 to 4 liters) of water over an hour or two; more than 32 ounces (about a liter) per hour is probably too much; too much water in brain cells increases pressure on your brain; early symptoms nausea, vomiting, headache; severe symptoms confusion, seizure, coma; water intoxication death is rare; risk rises with sports that make you sweat a lot over a long period; drink water when you're thirsty): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/water-intoxication

Mayo Clinic, 'Hyponatremia' (sodium helps regulate the amount of water in and around your cells; drinking excessive amounts of water can cause low sodium by overwhelming the kidneys' ability to excrete water; water levels rise and cells begin to swell; risk from drinking too much water during endurance activities such as marathons and triathlons; drinking water is vital for your health): https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/hyponatremia/symptoms-causes/syc-20373711

MedlinePlus (NIH NLM), 'Low blood sodium' (when sodium outside cells drops below normal, water moves into the cells and they swell; brain cells are especially sensitive to swelling): https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000394.htm

Cleveland Clinic, 'Hyponatremia' (severe hyponatremia can cause swelling in your tissues, including your brain; symptoms headache, nausea, confusion, seizures; use thirst as your guide for how much water to drink unless your provider tells you otherwise): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/17762-hyponatremia

Tease (next video): Cleveland Clinic, 'Is Cracking Your Knuckles Bad for You?' (the pop involves gas in the synovial fluid that lubricates finger joints; knuckle cracking won't cause arthritis): https://health.clevelandclinic.org/is-cracking-your-knuckles-bad-for-you

lines.text: What happens if you drink too much water?
Chug about a gallon in an hour or two,
and your brain can actually swell.
Sodium in your blood balances water in and around your cells.
lines.caps: *SODIUM | IN YOUR *BLOOD | *BALANCES WATER | IN AND *AROUND | YOUR *CELLS

lines.text: Your kidneys flush the extra, but only so fast.
Outrun them, and the water dilutes your sodium,
so water floods into your cells, and they swell.
lines.caps: SO WATER *FLOODS | INTO YOUR *CELLS | AND THEY *SWELL

lines.text: In your brain, that swelling builds pressure.
That means headaches, nausea, even confusion or seizures.
It's rare, but endurance athletes who overdo it are at risk.
lines.caps: IT'S *RARE | BUT *ENDURANCE | *ATHLETES | WHO *OVERDO IT | ARE AT *RISK

lines.text: So don't fear water. Just drink when you're thirsty.
